source.question: e-7112
source.value:
Let's denote the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ as $\mathbf{q}_1,\, \mathbf{q}_2,\,\mathbf{q}_3.$ 

Since $\mathcal{B}$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066805/assets/cfa33ba159e0627ec7a7288e44249acd88e0037e285fa786888dfcc13e5d538c.png) where $x_i = \dfrac{\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{q}_i}{\mathbf{q}_i \cdot \mathbf{q}_i}.$ 

Computing $x_2,$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{2}}{{q}_{2}\cdot {q}_{2}} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 1+6\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot (-4)}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4+6+8}{1+1+16} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

source.value:
Let's denote the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ as $\mathbf{q}_1,\, \mathbf{q}_2.$ 

Since $\mathcal{B}$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066805/assets/1ba0b151abea3c5b1a050c6ff924f3718fcb045b063b1b47df7a73f9d15316c9.png) where $x_i = \mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{q}_i.$ Computing the components of $\mathbf{x},$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}-2\sqrt{5} \\ 3\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]=-2-6=-8 \\ {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}-2\sqrt{5} \\ 3\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]=-4+3=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066805/assets/51184680e9ec8b56a437334ca2a9281b1b364da2c35922839be13e545d92cec4.png)
